reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Empleo, Desempleo y Subempleo (ENEMDU)
reports.description: Continuous household survey that is the primary source for labour-market indicators (adequate employment, underemployment, unemployment) and for income-based poverty and inequality measurement. National, urban and rural domains.
reports._notes: Central social and labour survey. Monthly and quarterly releases. Official source for both labour statistics and monetary poverty. Recent (Dec 2025): national poverty 21.4%, extreme poverty 8.3%; unemployment ~2.6–3.6%.

reports.title: Pobreza por ingresos y pobreza extrema / Income poverty
reports.description: Official income-poverty and extreme-poverty incidence, calculated by comparing household per-capita income (from ENEMDU) with nationally defined poverty lines updated by the IPC. Published with urban/rural breakdowns.
reports._notes: Headline social indicator. Dec 2025: national poverty 21.4% (down sharply from 28.0% a year earlier); extreme poverty 8.3%. Large urban–rural gap (urban ~13.8%, rural ~37.6%).

reports.title: Líneas de pobreza y pobreza extrema
reports.description: Monetary values of the poverty and extreme-poverty lines (per capita), updated with the IPC.
reports._notes: Direct input into the poverty measurement. Dec 2025: poverty line ~USD 92.40 per person; extreme poverty line ~USD 52.07.

reports.title: Índice de Precios al Consumidor (IPC) / Consumer Price Index
reports.description: Monthly consumer price index measuring changes in the prices of a representative basket of goods and services.
reports._notes: Flagship price statistic. Used to update the poverty lines and as the primary inflation indicator for the dollarized economy and for BCE analysis.

reports.title: Cuentas Nacionales / National Accounts of Ecuador
reports.description: System of national accounts producing GDP by production, expenditure and income. Quarterly and annual releases.
reports._notes: Core macroeconomic statistical system. In Ecuador the Banco Central plays a larger role in national accounts compilation than in pure INEI/DANE-style systems.

reports.title: Empleo adecuado / pleno empleo (ENEMDU)
reports.description: Key labour-market indicator from ENEMDU measuring the share of the employed who work full-time at or above the minimum wage. Central quality-of-employment metric in the Ecuadorian system.
reports._notes: Distinctive Ecuadorian labour indicator. Dec 2025: national adequate employment 37.1% (up from 33.0% a year earlier). Large urban–rural gap (urban ~46%, rural ~20%).

reports.title: Censo de Población y Vivienda / Population and Housing Census
reports.description: Decennial population and housing census. Provides the demographic baseline and sampling frames for household surveys.
reports._notes: Foundational demographic product. Continuously cited by ENEMDU design and poverty analysis.

reports.title: Coeficiente de Gini / Income inequality
reports.description: Official Gini coefficient of income inequality, calculated from the same ENEMDU income concept used for monetary poverty.
reports._notes: Companion inequality indicator to the poverty series. Recent values in the mid-0.44 to 0.47 range.

reports.title: Balanza de Pagos / Balance of Payments
reports.description: Quarterly and annual balance of payments covering the current account, capital/financial account and changes in reserve assets.
reports._notes: Core external-accounts product. 2025 current-account surplus reached a historical high of ~USD 7.7 bn, driven by the goods surplus and secondary income (remittances).

reports.title: Estadísticas de Comercio Exterior / Merchandise Trade
reports.description: Monthly and annual statistics of exports and imports of goods, with a sharp analytical split between oil and non-oil trade.
reports._notes: Trade data feed the BOP and national accounts. Non-oil exports (shrimp, cocoa, banana, mining) have become the main growth engine; oil remains important but has lost relative weight.

reports.title: Exportaciones e ingresos petroleros / Oil exports & fiscal contribution
reports.description: Statistics of crude-oil and derivatives production, exports and related fiscal revenues. Historically the dominant export and a major source of public revenue.
reports._notes: Structural but declining relative weight. 2025 oil exports ~USD 7.8 bn (down ~19% year-on-year). Still a key fiscal and external-sector variable, but non-oil exports now exceed oil by a wide margin.

reports.title: Exportaciones no petroleras (camarón, cacao, banano, minería)
reports.description: Non-oil merchandise exports, led by shrimp, cocoa & elaborates, banana/plantain and mining products. Principal recent driver of the trade surplus and of export diversification.
reports._notes: 2025 non-oil exports ~USD 29.4 bn (+18%). Shrimp, cocoa and banana are the headline traditional non-oil lines; mining has also grown. Central to the narrative of export diversification under dollarization.

reports.title: Reservas Internacionales del Banco Central del Ecuador
reports.description: Stock of international reserves managed by the central bank. Critical liquidity buffer in a fully dollarized economy.
reports._notes: Key external-buffer indicator under dollarization. End-2025 reserves reached record levels (~USD 9.8 bn). Cover deposits of the financial system and provide confidence in the dollarized regime.

reports.title: Régimen de dolarización oficial (desde 2000)
reports.publisher: Banco Central del Ecuador / Marco legal
reports.description: Official dollarization of the Ecuadorian economy (US dollar as legal tender since 2000). Defines the monetary regime: no independent national currency or classic policy interest rate.
reports._notes: Foundational institutional regime node. Continuously cited as the framework that constrains monetary policy and elevates the importance of fiscal discipline, reserves and external competitiveness.
_referenced_by: Every major BCE macroeconomic and monetary report
Analysis of inflation, reserves and financial stability

reports.title: Índice Nacional de Precios al Productor (INPP)
reports.description: Monthly producer price index, published with and without oil. Measures price changes at the producer level across agriculture, mining, manufacturing and utilities.
reports._notes: Complements the IPC. The oil/non-oil split mirrors the trade and production analysis. Useful for cost-push and industrial-price monitoring.

reports.title: Canasta Familiar Básica y Canasta Familiar Vital
reports.description: Official cost of the basic and vital family baskets, published monthly with the IPC. Used for living-cost and wage-reference analysis.
reports._notes: High-visibility living-cost indicator. Linked to the IPC and frequently cited in wage and social-policy discussion.

reports.title: Remesas de trabajadores / Secondary income (remittances)
reports.description: Statistics of worker remittances received from abroad. Major component of the secondary-income account and a stabilising factor in the balance of payments.
reports._notes: Structurally important inflow. Contributed to the record current-account surplus in 2025. Complements the goods-trade surplus in the external accounts.

reports.title: Camarón, cacao y banano — leading non-oil export products
reports.description: Product-level export statistics for the three largest non-oil traditional export lines: shrimp, cocoa & elaborates, and banana/plantain.
reports._notes: These three products dominate non-oil traditional exports. Shrimp has overtaken oil in some recent periods as the single largest export earner; cocoa has seen exceptional value growth.

reports.title: Quito / Distrito Metropolitano de Quito — capital statistical identity
reports.description: Capital city and primary highland urban economy. Core of Pichincha province. Lower income-poverty incidence than the national average.
reports._notes: Dominant highland metro. Pichincha records among the lowest provincial income-poverty rates (~11%). Continuously published as a key urban domain in ENEMDU labour and poverty analysis.

reports.title: Guayaquil / Área metropolitana de Guayaquil — coastal statistical identity
reports.description: Largest coastal city and main commercial/port economy. Core of Guayas province. Intermediate-to-higher poverty incidence relative to the capital.
reports._notes: Dominant coastal metro. Guayas carries a large absolute number of poor households. Completes the capital–port-city contrast inside the national urban hierarchy.

reports.title: Provincia de Pichincha — low-poverty contrast
reports.description: Highland province containing Quito. Among the lowest income-poverty rates in the 2025 provincial results.
reports._notes: 2025 income poverty ~11.2%. Completes the low-poverty pole opposite the Amazonian and some coastal provinces.

reports.title: Provincia de Morona Santiago — highest-poverty Amazon contrast
reports.description: Amazonian province with the highest income-poverty incidence in recent provincial results. Tests the statistical hierarchy under extreme marginalisation.
reports._notes: Poverty-contrast province. 2025 income poverty reported in the mid-70% range; also among the highest in multidimensional and NBI poverty. National survey infrastructure reaches the province; local independent statistical density is thin.

reports.title: Provincia de Orellana — high-poverty Amazon contrast
reports.description: Amazonian oil-producing province that previously recorded the highest poverty rates and saw a sharp decline in 2025.
reports._notes: 2025 income poverty fell dramatically (from ~76% to ~44%). Illustrates both the high-poverty Amazon cluster and the volatility of provincial estimates in smaller domains.

reports.title: Pobreza por ingresos por provincia (INEC)
reports.description: Official provincial tabulations of income poverty and related indicators. Primary source for the inter-provincial poverty gradient.
reports._notes: Key homogeneity-test product. 2025 ranking extremes: Morona Santiago highest; Tungurahua and Pichincha among the lowest (~11%). National average ~21.8%.

reports.title: Acuerdo Comercial Ecuador–Unión Europea
reports.description: Trade agreement with the European Union providing preferential access for Ecuadorian exports (especially banana, shrimp, cocoa, flowers). One of the most important preferential markets.
reports._notes: Major preferential instrument. Continuously cited in official trade-performance reporting; EU ranks among the top destinations for non-oil exports.
_referenced_by: Export statistics by partner (EU is a top destination for non-oil exports)
Policy analysis of preferential market access

reports.title: Acuerdo Comercial Ecuador–China
reports.publisher: Gobierno del Ecuador / República Popular China
reports.description: Trade agreement with China providing preferential access and underpinning growing bilateral trade, especially in non-oil exports and imports of manufactures.
reports._notes: Important bilateral instrument. China is a top destination for non-oil exports; the agreement is routinely cited in diversification analysis.
_referenced_by: Official monitoring of the China agreement

reports.title: Presupuesto General del Estado / National Budget
reports.description: Annual national budget law and subsequent execution reports covering revenues (including oil) and expenditure of the central government.
reports._notes: Operational fiscal framework. Links oil and non-oil revenues with functional spending on education, health, social protection and investment. Critical under dollarization because monetary financing is constrained.

reports.title: Cuentas Satélite de Educación (CSE)
reports.description: Satellite accounts of education measuring the value added, expenditure and production of the education sector (public and private). Complements the national accounts with a sectoral view of education.
reports._notes: 2024 education VAB ~5.5% of GDP (USD 6.8 bn). Higher education is the largest single industry within the satellite. Links the education budget to the real-side accounts.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGHUR)
reports.description: Periodic household income and expenditure survey. Updates the structure of household consumption, provides the weights for the IPC, and supports living-conditions and inequality analysis.
reports._notes: Structural survey (latest 2024-2025 after a 12-year gap). Average monthly household income ~USD 1,135; expenditure ~USD 930. Directly feeds the IPC basket and complements ENEMDU on the expenditure side.

reports.title: Pobreza por Necesidades Básicas Insatisfechas (NBI)
reports.description: Structural poverty indicator based on unsatisfied basic needs (housing quality, overcrowding, access to services, education, economic dependence). Calculated primarily from census data and updated with survey information.
reports._notes: Complementary structural poverty measure to income poverty. 2022 census: 39.8% of the population with at least one NBI. Provincial extremes remain large (Amazonian provinces highest).

reports.title: Instituto Ecuatoriano de Seguridad Social (IESS) — coverage and finances
reports.description: Main social-security institution covering pensions, health insurance and other benefits for formal workers and their dependents. Major fiscal counterpart and health-system actor.
reports._notes: Central social-protection node. Large and growing claims on the national budget (state contribution to pensions and health). Continuously cited in fiscal and health-system analysis; historical arrears are a recurring policy issue.

reports.title: Sistema de salud pública / Ministry of Health statistics
reports.description: Public-health service statistics, coverage indicators and related expenditure. Complements IESS and household-survey health modules.
reports._notes: Public provider side of the dual health system (MSP + IESS). Linked to the health functional budget and to household access indicators from ENEMDU/ENIGHUR.

reports.title: Gasto público en educación
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / INEC CSE
reports.description: Public expenditure on education as reflected in the national budget and in the education satellite accounts.
reports._notes: Education is a constitutionally prioritised function. CSE and budget execution together track the resource side of the education system.

reports.title: Gasto público en salud y seguridad social
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / IESS
reports.description: Public expenditure on health and social security, including the state contribution to IESS pensions and health benefits.
reports._notes: Health and social-security spending are major and growing budget items. The state–IESS financing relationship is a structural fiscal issue under dollarization.

reports.title: Encuesta Nacional sobre Desnutrición Infantil (ENDI)
reports.description: Specialised survey on child malnutrition, early childhood development and related household conditions. Complements the broader health and living-conditions system.
reports._notes: High-priority social indicator survey. Tracks chronic malnutrition and early-childhood development outcomes; used for targeted social-policy monitoring.

reports.title: Provincia de Tungurahua — low-poverty highland contrast
reports.description: Highland province with among the lowest income-poverty rates in the 2025 results. Completes the low-poverty set alongside Pichincha.
reports._notes: 2025 income poverty ~11%. Useful as a second low-poverty highland node.

reports.title: Provincia de Manabí — large coastal province
reports.description: Major coastal province with elevated poverty and a large absolute number of poor households. Completes the coastal provincial set alongside Guayas.
reports._notes: Significant coastal population and poverty mass. Frequently appears in both absolute and relative poverty rankings.

reports.title: Camarón — producción y exportaciones
reports.publisher: Cámara Nacional de Acuacultura / BCE / INEC
reports.description: Statistics of shrimp aquaculture production and exports. Ecuador’s leading export product by value, surpassing oil in recent years. Concentrated in Guayas and other coastal provinces.
reports._notes: Structural export success story. 2025 exports reached record levels (~USD 8.4 bn), overtaking oil as the single largest export earner. ~225–230k hectares in production; major employment generator (especially female labour). China, EU and US are the main markets.

reports.title: Sector acuícola / Aquaculture statistics
reports.publisher: Cámara Nacional de Acuacultura / MAG / BCE
reports.description: Broader aquaculture sector statistics, dominated by shrimp but also covering other cultured species. Complements the product-level shrimp series.
reports._notes: Industry association and official statistics track production area, employment, export volumes and values. Guayas accounts for ~60% of shrimp production area.

reports.title: Servicio de Rentas Internas (SRI) — tax collection
reports.description: National tax administration. Publishes gross tax collection by type of tax (VAT, income tax, ICE, etc.) and performance against annual targets.
reports._notes: Primary non-oil revenue-side fiscal statistic. 2025 collection ~USD 21.5 bn (record). VAT is the largest single tax. Critical under dollarization because monetary financing is unavailable.

reports.title: Impuesto al Valor Agregado (IVA) / Value-added tax
reports.description: Main consumption tax. Rate and base changes are high-visibility fiscal policy instruments; collection is published monthly by the SRI.
reports._notes: Largest single tax revenue. Recent rate/base adjustments (including expansion of the taxable base) have been material drivers of collection growth.

reports.title: Deuda pública / Public debt statistics
reports.publisher: Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas / BCE
reports.description: Stock and flow statistics of central-government and public-sector debt (external and domestic). Key sustainability indicator under dollarization.
reports._notes: Critical fiscal-sustainability node. Continuously monitored because dollarization removes the option of monetary financing of deficits.

reports.title: Provincia de El Oro — shrimp and coastal production
reports.description: Coastal province that is the second-largest shrimp-producing area after Guayas. Completes the coastal aquaculture geography.
reports._notes: ~15% of national shrimp production area. Links the commodity (shrimp) to the provincial production and poverty geography.

reports.title: Provincia de Esmeraldas — northern coastal contrast
reports.description: Northern coastal province with elevated poverty and a significant share of shrimp and other coastal production.
reports._notes: Elevated poverty incidence relative to the highland core. Completes the set of major coastal provinces (Guayas, Manabí, El Oro, Esmeraldas).

reports.title: Cacao y elaborados — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of cocoa production and exports (beans and elaborates). One of the three leading non-oil traditional export products alongside shrimp and banana.
reports._notes: Strong recent value growth. Completes the product-level view of the non-oil traditional export triad (shrimp–cocoa–banana).

reports.title: Banano y plátano — producción y exportaciones
reports.description: Statistics of banana and plantain production and exports. Long-standing traditional export and a major employer in coastal provinces.
reports._notes: Classic traditional export. Still a large volume and value line; frequently cited alongside shrimp and cocoa in non-oil export analysis.

reports.title: Provincia del Guayas — core coastal statistical identity
reports.description: Largest coastal province, containing Guayaquil and the majority of national shrimp production area. Intermediate-to-higher poverty incidence and the largest absolute poverty mass.
reports._notes: ~60% of shrimp production area; hosts the main port and commercial economy. Completes the provincial set with the largest economic and demographic weight on the coast.

dependencies.basis: Income poverty is calculated from ENEMDU household income data.
Poverty status is determined by comparing per-capita income with the official poverty lines.
Poverty lines are updated with the IPC.
The Gini coefficient is computed from the same income distribution underlying the poverty estimates.
Merchandise trade flows are a primary input into the goods account of the balance of payments.
The basic and vital baskets are priced with the same price data underlying the IPC.
The EU agreement underpins preferential access for major non-oil exports.
The China agreement underpins growing bilateral trade flows.
Oil revenues remain a material component of the national budget.
ENIGHUR provides the expenditure weights for the IPC basket.
NBI is calculated primarily from census housing, education and service variables.
Tax collection is the primary non-oil revenue source of the national budget.
Guayas accounts for the majority of national shrimp production area.
El Oro is the second-largest shrimp-producing province.

ENDI does not use Ministry of Health statistics: INEC's 'Documento Metodologico ENDI' builds its sample from the household Marco Maestro de Muestreo (2010 pre-censo plus 2011-2018 cartographic updating), and the MSP appears only as a provider of methodological/training support and blood-sampling facilities, and in the users table ('Ministerio de Salud Publica: Informacion actualizada que de cuenta del impacto de los programas'). The flow runs the other way: the MSP publishes the national chronic child malnutrition figure sourced to ENDI — 'La medicion reflejo tambien que... se ha reducido esta problematica en 3,5 %, pasando del 23,6 % de menores de dos anos con DCI al 20,1 %', from 'la primera Encuesta Especializada sobre Desnutricion Infantil (ENDI) 2022-2023... la encuesta disenada por el Instituto Ecuatoriano de Estadistica y Censos (INEC)'.
